title: Self-Hosted Model Update, Rollback, and Incident Playbook
summary: Qualify complete serving-unit changes, release with bounded exposure, roll back on a forced gate failure, and recover incidents through evidence-based closure.
prerequisites: A verified known-good serving-unit manifest and reproducible artifacts
Candidate qualification gates, human release authority, and bounded rollout controls
Incident roles, communication paths, recovery objectives, and an evidence-retention policy

sections.title: Qualify and release the complete change
paragraphs: Diff the complete serving unit: model and tokenizer, runtime and drivers, image and dependencies, templates and adapters, endpoint behavior, gateway, identity and policy, networks and secrets, infrastructure, evaluation, load profile, telemetry, cost, state compatibility, and runbooks. Classify each change and hidden dependency; a model-only comparison misses many of the boundaries that determine real behavior.

Rebuild or retrieve immutable artifacts, verify provenance and license, rerun affected and regression evaluation slices, replay representative load and failure cases, confirm observability and cost, validate backward and rollback compatibility, and obtain authorized human disposition. Warm the candidate before traffic and release with bounded cohort, time, request, concurrency, cost, and error exposure.

sections.title: Roll back and respond through verified postconditions
paragraphs: Predeclare hard stop and rollback triggers. When a trigger fires, stop or limit new work, preserve exact routing and build evidence, drain or cancel safely, reconcile requests and external effects whose outcome is unknown, and restore the complete compatible known-good unit. Verify model identity, authorization, endpoint behavior, important quality and safety checks, queues, telemetry, cost, and user-visible postconditions before declaring recovery.

For an incident, lead with impact and uncertainty. Assign authority, severity, timeline, affected users and work, narrow containment, evidence handling, communication cadence, and recovery objectives. Diagnose the responsible model, application, adapter, policy, data, tool, gateway, infrastructure, or operational boundary. Close only after recovery is stable, affected work is reconciled, required notices are complete, residual risks are accepted by authorized humans, and prevention work has an owner and date.

code.label: Update, rollback, and incident record
code.code:
Task: [CHANGE OR INCIDENT AND PROTECTED OUTCOME]
Scope: [USERS/WORK, COMPLETE SERVING UNIT, ROUTING, STATE, TOOLS/EFFECTS, INFRASTRUCTURE, AND TIME WINDOW]
Permissions: [QUALIFY, APPROVE, ROUTE, STOP, ROLLBACK, ACCESS EVIDENCE, COMMUNICATE, AND CLOSE]
Exact build: [BASELINE AND CANDIDATE MODEL/IMAGE/RUNTIME/DRIVER/ADAPTER/POLICY/CONFIG/EVAL DIGESTS]
Release bounds: [COHORT, TIME, REQUEST, CONCURRENCY, COST, ERROR, AND AUTOMATIC/HUMAN STOP]
Incident ledger: [DETECTION, SEVERITY, IMPACT, UNCERTAINTY, TIMELINE, CONTAINMENT, EVIDENCE, COMMUNICATION, AND OWNER]
Verification: [CANDIDATE GATES, FORCED FAILURE, ROUTING, DRAIN/CANCEL, STATE RECONCILIATION, RESTORED POSTCONDITIONS, AND RECOVERY OBJECTIVES]
Stop conditions: [HARD GATE, UNAUTHORIZED EFFECT, DATA/SECURITY EVENT, CAPACITY/COST LIMIT, UNKNOWN OUTCOME WITHOUT RECONCILIATION, OR FAILED RESTORE]
Recovery: [STOP/LIMIT, CONTAIN, RECONCILE, RESTORE COMPLETE KNOWN-GOOD UNIT, VERIFY, COMMUNICATE, ACCEPT RESIDUAL RISK, OWN PREVENTION]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes baseline and candidate manifests, artifact and provenance verification, complete diff and compatibility decision, evaluation and load comparison, approvals, bounded routing, forced failed-gate evidence, rollback timeline, state and side-effect reconciliation, restored postconditions, incident ledger, recovery-objective results, communications, residual-risk acceptance, prevention owners, and next exercise date.

Do not close because one health check turns green or a model reports success. Stop on any hard gate, unauthorized or unknown external effect, security or data event, uncontrolled capacity or cost, unreconciled outcome, or failed restore. Maintain containment, reconcile affected work, restore or rebuild from verified artifacts, repeat access, quality, load, telemetry, and user-visible checks, communicate status, and close only with accountable human evidence.

sections.title: Evidence boundaries and authoritative references
paragraphs: This supplement distinguishes three evidence classes. ACTUAL LOCAL OBSERVATION means output a learner personally obtains by running the supplied files. No local execution is claimed during authoring, so every output shown below is proposed expected output. FICTIONAL CLASSROOM VALUE means an invented identifier, score, owner, timestamp, limit, lookup result, approval, or incident result that is explicitly used for teaching. UNKNOWN DEPLOYMENT QUALIFICATION means that no evidence here establishes the safety, compatibility, capacity, licensing, authorization, or recoverability of a real deployment.

The simulator is an offline state machine. It does not deploy a model, change Kubernetes resources, call a gateway, query an identity provider, inspect a queue, produce an external effect, or exercise a real human approval system. Kubernetes documents Deployment rollout and rollback behavior at https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/, but a production adapter must still map this procedure to actual controllers, routing, persistent state, evidence stores, and authorization boundaries.

SLSA documents provenance at https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/provenance. Provenance can identify how an artifact was produced, but it does not establish operational compatibility or deployment authorization. OpenTelemetry semantic conventions are documented at https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/. Prometheus Alertmanager documents alert grouping, routing, inhibition, and silencing at https://prometheus.io/docs/alerting/latest/alertmanager/. NIST incident-response recommendations are available at https://www.nist.gov/publications/incident-response-recommendations-and-considerations-cybersecurity-risk-management-csf.

The scripts use Python frozen data classes and unittest. Their standard-library behavior is documented at https://docs.python.org/3/library/dataclasses.html and https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html. These documentation links do not prove that the proposed scripts were locally executed.

code.label: Evidence classification
code.code:
ACTUAL LOCAL OBSERVATION: Output obtained after the learner runs the supplied files.
FICTIONAL CLASSROOM VALUE: Every incident value, lookup result, limit, timestamp, owner, or authority fixture labeled fictional.
UNKNOWN DEPLOYMENT QUALIFICATION: Whether any real serving unit is safe, compatible, licensed, authorized, capacity-tested, or recoverable.

A proposed expected output becomes an actual local observation only for the person and environment that produced it.

sections.title: Complete serving unit, release bounds, and stop conditions
paragraphs: A rollback must address the complete serving unit, not only its model file. The supplied simulator therefore gives each immutable manifest explicit model, tokenizer, runtime, driver, image, dependency, template, adapter, endpoint, gateway, identity, policy, network, secret-reference, infrastructure, configuration, evaluation, load-profile, telemetry, cost-profile, state-schema, and runbook fields. Secret references are identifiers, not secret values.

The fictional baseline is baseline-2026-09-01 with model model-baseline-2026-09-01, tokenizer tok-7, runtime runtime-4, driver driver-12, image image-sha256-fictional-a1, adapter adapter-a, endpoint schema-3, policy policy-7, and state schema state-5. The fictional candidate is candidate-2026-09-20 with model model-candidate-2026-09-20 and the same remaining components. Its fictional safety score is 0.91 against a required minimum of 0.95.

The fictional release limits are cohort at most 10 percent, at most 20 admitted requests, at most 15 elapsed minutes, concurrency at most 2, cost at most 5 credits, and error rate at most 2 percent. The simulator checks prospective exposure before admitting a request. An operation that failed before an effect is retained in the incident ledger, but it is not automatically classified as an error in the separate release-bound metric. A real adapter must define that metric precisely.

Stop conditions are a hard gate failure, unauthorized effect, data or security event, capacity or cost limit, unknown effect without authoritative reconciliation, or failed restore. Exceeding any release bound rejects further admission. A hard gate failure also requires the incident procedure, even if exposure remains below every numerical limit.

code.label: Fictional release contract
code.code:
cohort_percent <= 10
admitted_requests <= 20
elapsed_minutes <= 15
concurrency <= 2
cost_credits <= 5
error_rate_percent <= 2

AUTOMATIC STOP: hard gate, unauthorized effect, data/security event, exposure violation, unreconciled effect, or failed restore
HUMAN REQUIREMENT: release authorization and incident closure are separate decisions

sections.title: Completed worked input: fictional candidate gate incident
paragraphs: Incident FICTIONAL-2026-09-20-017 is a classroom record, not a real deployment report. The protected outcome was to prevent unsafe candidate traffic, preserve request effects, and restore the complete known-good serving unit. Fictional roles were incident commander Priya Shah, release manager Mateo Ruiz, service operator Lin Chen, application owner Dana Okafor, evidence custodian Noor Haddad, and communications lead Jules Martin.

The candidate received 5 admitted requests within a prepared 8-request classroom cohort. Three completed, one failed before an external effect, and operation op-103 had an unknown effect. The remaining 3 were not admitted. The release-bound error metric did not classify the failed-before-effect operation as an endpoint error. This is a fictional metric definition and must not be copied into production without an accountable local specification.

The fictional timeline uses minutes after 09:03 detection: minute 0, corresponding to 09:03, critical safety gate failure recorded; minute 1, 09:04, admission stopped; minute 2, 09:05, routing and build evidence preserved; minute 4, 09:07, admitted work drained; minute 6, 09:09, op-103 reconciled by stable identity using a fictional authoritative lookup; minute 8, 09:11, the compatible complete baseline restored; minute 9, 09:12, recovery postconditions passed and restoration was communicated. The completed worked record ends with incident closure pending because actual human authority is absent. A fictional positive-authority value appears only in a separately labeled test fixture and does not confer actual authorization.

The service-recovery target was at most 10 minutes from detection. The fictional ledger reports recovery in 9 minutes, so the target was met by 1 minute. This arithmetic is a classroom result, not a measured recovery objective for real infrastructure.

The diagnosed initiating failure was the candidate safety gate because 0.91 was below 0.95. It was not diagnosed as a gateway, policy, state-schema, or generic health failure. The release manager withheld candidate release approval. Service restoration was communicated at 09:12, while incident closure remained pending. The separate fictional positive-authority test demonstrates a possible closure transition at minute 12 but is not part of the worked record and is not actual authorization.

sections.title: Concrete rollback and incident procedure
paragraphs: Follow this enforced order. First, record the exact candidate, baseline, routing, exposure, clock, and trigger. Second, stop admission. Third, preserve manifests, logs, alerts, routing, operation identities, and approval state. Fourth, drain or safely cancel admitted work. Fifth, reconcile every unknown effect by stable operation identity. A missing lookup result leaves the operation on HOLD. Sixth, compare endpoint, state, authorization, and other rollback-critical contracts. Seventh, restore the complete compatible baseline. Eighth, evaluate each recovery postcondition from supplied evidence. Ninth, communicate service restoration. Tenth, close only after an authorized human accepts residual risk, required notices are complete, and prevention has an owner and due date.

The simulator enforces phase order. Restore cannot run before state recording, admission stop, evidence preservation, drain, and reconciliation. Incompatibility and restore failure return controlled failure results while containment remains active and recovered remains false. They are not represented only by assertions.

Recovery and closure are separate. Successful recovery does not approve the failed candidate. The primary runnable example restores service but leaves closure pending because actual human authority is absent. A separately labeled fictional positive authority fixture exists only to test the closure transition.

A production incident commander must communicate impact and uncertainty, retain evidence according to local policy, identify affected users and work, establish communication cadence, and assign residual-risk and prevention decisions to authorized people. UNKNOWN must not be converted to success merely to advance the state machine.

3. PRESERVE: manifests, routing, ledger, gate evidence, and authority state at minute 2
4. DRAIN: admitted work at minute 4
5. RECONCILE: op-103 by stable identity at minute 6
6. COMPATIBILITY: endpoint schema-3, state-5, and policy-7 agree

9. COMMUNICATE: service restored; closure still pending

sections.title: Runnable deterministic offline simulator
paragraphs: Save the following block exactly as rollback_simulator.py. It requires Python 3.11 or later and uses only the standard library. It performs no network access, creates no temporary directory, writes no files, and deletes nothing.

The simulator accepts explicit fictional recovery evidence instead of manufacturing green gates. Effect reconciliation accepts an explicit lookup mapping. A missing mapping leaves the unknown operation on HOLD. Restore requires prior containment phases, successful reconciliation, compatibility, and an explicit restore-result input.
Release approval is never inferred from recovery. The candidate_release_approved field remains false in the worked example. Incident closure requires separate closure evidence.

code.label: rollback_simulator.py
code.code:
from dataclasses import dataclass, fields, replace
from enum import Enum, auto
from math import isfinite
from numbers import Integral, Real


def require_nonnegative_real(name, value):
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, Real):
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a finite nonnegative number")
    if not isfinite(float(value)) or value < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a finite nonnegative number")


def require_nonnegative_integer(name, value):
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, Integral) or value < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a nonnegative integer")


def require_exact_bools(instance, names):
    for name in names:
        if type(getattr(instance, name)) is not bool:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be bool")


class TransitionError(RuntimeError):
    pass


class ExposureLimit(RuntimeError):
    pass


class Phase(Enum):
    NEW = auto()
    RECORDED = auto()
    STOPPED = auto()
    PRESERVED = auto()
    DRAINED = auto()
    RECONCILED = auto()
    RESTORED = auto()
    RECOVERED = auto()
    COMMUNICATED = auto()
    CLOSED = auto()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Manifest:
    identity: str
    model: str
    tokenizer: str
    runtime: str
    driver: str
    image_digest: str
    dependencies_digest: str
    prompt_template: str
    adapter: str
    endpoint_schema: str
    gateway_route: str
    identity_provider: str
    authorization_policy: str
    network_policy: str
    secret_reference: str
    infrastructure_profile: str
    configuration_digest: str
    evaluation_suite: str
    load_profile: str
    telemetry_config: str
    cost_profile: str
    state_schema: str
    runbook: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReleaseBounds:
    cohort_percent: float = 10.0
    max_requests: int = 20
    max_minutes: int = 15
    max_concurrency: int = 2
    max_cost_credits: float = 5.0
    max_error_percent: float = 2.0

    def __post_init__(self):
        require_nonnegative_real("cohort_percent", self.cohort_percent)
        require_nonnegative_integer("max_requests", self.max_requests)
        require_nonnegative_real("max_minutes", self.max_minutes)
        require_nonnegative_integer("max_concurrency", self.max_concurrency)
        require_nonnegative_real("max_cost_credits", self.max_cost_credits)
        require_nonnegative_real("max_error_percent", self.max_error_percent)


@dataclass
class Exposure:
    requests: int = 0
    errors: int = 0
    cost_credits: float = 0.0


@dataclass
class Operation:
    identity: str
    outcome: str
    effect_reconciled: bool


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RecoveryEvidence:
    identity: bool
    authorization: bool
    endpoint: bool
    quality: bool
    safety: bool
    queue: bool
    telemetry: bool
    cost: bool
    visible_state: bool

    def __post_init__(self):
        require_exact_bools(self, (
            "identity", "authorization", "endpoint", "quality", "safety",
            "queue", "telemetry", "cost", "visible_state"
        ))


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ClosureEvidence:
    human_authority: bool
    residual_risk_accepted: bool
    required_notices_complete: bool
    prevention_owner: str
    prevention_due: str

    def __post_init__(self):
        require_exact_bools(self, (
            "human_authority", "residual_risk_accepted",
            "required_notices_complete"
        ))
        if not isinstance(self.prevention_owner, str):
            raise ValueError("prevention_owner must be str")
        if not isinstance(self.prevention_due, str):
            raise ValueError("prevention_due must be str")


BASELINE = Manifest(
    "baseline-2026-09-01", "model-baseline-2026-09-01", "tok-7",
    "runtime-4", "driver-12", "image-sha256-fictional-a1",
    "deps-sha256-fictional-d1", "template-3", "adapter-a", "schema-3",
    "route-blue", "identity-2", "policy-7", "network-4", "secret-ref-6",
    "infra-8", "config-sha256-fictional-c1", "eval-11", "load-5",
    "telemetry-2", "cost-3", "state-5", "runbook-9"
)
CANDIDATE = replace(
    BASELINE,
    identity="candidate-2026-09-20",
    model="model-candidate-2026-09-20"
)
GOOD_RECOVERY_EVIDENCE = RecoveryEvidence(
    True, True, True, True, True, True, True, True, True
)
FICTIONAL_AUTHORITY_POSITIVE = ClosureEvidence(
    True, True, True, "Dana Okafor", "2026-09-27"
)
MISSING_ACTUAL_AUTHORITY = ClosureEvidence(
    False, False, False, "", ""
)


class Simulation:
    def __init__(self, candidate=CANDIDATE, operations=None, bounds=None):
        self.baseline = BASELINE
        self.candidate = candidate
        self.service_unit = candidate
        self.operations = operations or [
            Operation("op-101", "completed", True),
            Operation("op-102", "failed", True),
            Operation("op-103", "unknown", False),
            Operation("op-104", "completed", True),
            Operation("op-105", "completed", True),
        ]
        self.bounds = bounds or ReleaseBounds()
        self.exposure = Exposure()
        self.phase = Phase.NEW
        self.minute = 0
        self.events = []
        self.admission_open = True
        self.contained = False
        self.recovered = False
        self.incident_closed = False
        self.candidate_release_approved = False
        self.diagnosis = None
        self.gates = {}

    def validate_event_time(self, minute):
        require_nonnegative_real("minute", minute)
        if minute < self.minute:
            raise TransitionError("time cannot move backward")

    def at(self, minute, event):
        self.validate_event_time(minute)
        self.minute = minute
        self.events.append((minute, event))

    def require(self, phase):
        if self.phase is not phase:
            raise TransitionError(
                f"required phase {phase.name}, found {self.phase.name}"
            )

    def admit(self, *, cohort_percent, elapsed_minutes, concurrency,
              cost_credits, is_error=False):
        require_nonnegative_real("cohort_percent", cohort_percent)
        require_nonnegative_real("elapsed_minutes", elapsed_minutes)
        require_nonnegative_integer("concurrency", concurrency)
        require_nonnegative_real("cost_credits", cost_credits)
        if type(is_error) is not bool:
            raise ValueError("is_error must be bool")
        if not self.admission_open:
            raise ExposureLimit("admission is stopped")
        requests = self.exposure.requests + 1
        errors = self.exposure.errors + int(is_error)
        cost = self.exposure.cost_credits + cost_credits
        error_percent = 100.0 * errors / requests
        violations = []
        if cohort_percent > self.bounds.cohort_percent:
            violations.append("cohort")
        if requests > self.bounds.max_requests:
            violations.append("requests")
        if elapsed_minutes > self.bounds.max_minutes:
            violations.append("time")
        if concurrency > self.bounds.max_concurrency:
            violations.append("concurrency")
        if cost > self.bounds.max_cost_credits:
            violations.append("cost")
        if error_percent > self.bounds.max_error_percent:
            violations.append("error_rate")
        if violations:
            self.admission_open = False
            self.contained = True
            raise ExposureLimit("release bound exceeded: " + ",".join(violations))
        self.exposure.requests = requests
        self.exposure.errors = errors
        self.exposure.cost_credits = cost

    def trigger_critical_gate(self, score, minimum):
        if score >= minimum:
            raise ValueError("critical gate did not fail")
        self.diagnosis = "candidate_safety_gate"
        self.events.append((self.minute, "critical_gate_failed"))

    def record_state(self, minute):
        self.require(Phase.NEW)
        if self.diagnosis is None:
            raise TransitionError("trigger must be recorded first")
        self.at(minute, "state_recorded")
        self.phase = Phase.RECORDED

    def stop_admission(self, minute):
        self.require(Phase.RECORDED)
        self.at(minute, "admission_stopped")
        self.admission_open = False
        self.contained = True
        self.phase = Phase.STOPPED

    def preserve_evidence(self, minute):
        self.require(Phase.STOPPED)
        self.at(minute, "evidence_preserved")
        self.phase = Phase.PRESERVED

    def drain(self, minute):
        self.require(Phase.PRESERVED)
        if self.admission_open:
            raise TransitionError("cannot drain while admission is open")
        self.at(minute, "work_drained")
        self.phase = Phase.DRAINED

    def reconcile_effects(self, lookup, minute):
        self.require(Phase.DRAINED)
        self.validate_event_time(minute)
        unknown = [op for op in self.operations if op.outcome == "unknown"]
        missing = [op.identity for op in unknown if op.identity not in lookup]
        if missing:
            self.at(minute, "effect_hold:" + ",".join(missing))
            return False
        for op in unknown:
            resolved = lookup[op.identity]
            if resolved not in {"completed", "absent"}:
                raise ValueError("lookup result must be completed or absent")
        for op in unknown:
            resolved = lookup[op.identity]
            op.outcome = "completed" if resolved == "completed" else "failed"
            op.effect_reconciled = True
        self.at(minute, "effects_reconciled")
        self.phase = Phase.RECONCILED
        return True

    def compatible(self, baseline=None, candidate=None):
        baseline = baseline or self.baseline
        candidate = candidate or self.candidate
        critical = (
            "tokenizer", "runtime", "driver", "endpoint_schema",
            "authorization_policy", "state_schema", "configuration_digest"
        )
        return all(getattr(baseline, name) == getattr(candidate, name)
                   for name in critical)

    def restore(self, restore_succeeded, minute):
        self.require(Phase.RECONCILED)
        self.validate_event_time(minute)
        if type(restore_succeeded) is not bool:
            raise ValueError("restore_succeeded must be bool")
        if not self.compatible():
            self.at(minute, "restore_refused_incompatible")
            return False
        if not restore_succeeded:
            self.at(minute, "restore_failed")
            return False
        self.service_unit = self.baseline
        self.at(minute, "complete_baseline_restored")
        self.phase = Phase.RESTORED
        return True

    def verify_postconditions(self, evidence, minute):
        self.require(Phase.RESTORED)
        self.validate_event_time(minute)
        if not isinstance(evidence, RecoveryEvidence):
            raise ValueError("evidence must be RecoveryEvidence")
        require_exact_bools(evidence, (
            "identity", "authorization", "endpoint", "quality", "safety",
            "queue", "telemetry", "cost", "visible_state"
        ))
        all_effects_known = all(
            op.effect_reconciled and op.outcome in {"completed", "failed"}
            for op in self.operations
        )
        self.gates = {
            "identity": evidence.identity and self.service_unit == self.baseline,
            "authorization": evidence.authorization and
                             self.service_unit.authorization_policy == "policy-7",
            "endpoint": evidence.endpoint and
                        self.service_unit.endpoint_schema == "schema-3",
            "quality": evidence.quality,
            "safety": evidence.safety,
            "queue": evidence.queue and all_effects_known,
            "telemetry": evidence.telemetry,
            "cost": evidence.cost,
            "visible_state": evidence.visible_state,
        }
        self.at(minute, "postconditions_evaluated")
        if not all(self.gates.values()):
            return False
        self.recovered = True
        self.phase = Phase.RECOVERED
        return True

    def communicate_restoration(self, minute):
        self.require(Phase.RECOVERED)
        self.at(minute, "restoration_communicated")
        self.phase = Phase.COMMUNICATED

    def close_incident(self, evidence, minute):
        self.require(Phase.COMMUNICATED)
        self.validate_event_time(minute)
        if not isinstance(evidence, ClosureEvidence):
            raise ValueError("evidence must be ClosureEvidence")
        require_exact_bools(evidence, (
            "human_authority", "residual_risk_accepted",
            "required_notices_complete"
        ))
        complete = (
            evidence.human_authority and
            evidence.residual_risk_accepted and
            evidence.required_notices_complete and
            bool(evidence.prevention_owner.strip()) and
            bool(evidence.prevention_due.strip())
        )
        self.at(minute, "closure_evaluated")
        if not complete:
            return False
        self.incident_closed = True
        self.phase = Phase.CLOSED
        return True


def make_contained_sim(candidate=CANDIDATE, operations=None):
    sim = Simulation(candidate=candidate, operations=operations)
    sim.trigger_critical_gate(0.91, 0.95)
    sim.record_state(0)
    sim.stop_admission(1)
    sim.preserve_evidence(2)
    sim.drain(4)
    return sim


def main():
    sim = Simulation()
    for elapsed in range(5):
        sim.admit(cohort_percent=10.0, elapsed_minutes=elapsed,
                  concurrency=1, cost_credits=0.5, is_error=False)
    print("START candidate=" + sim.candidate.identity)
    print("BOUNDS requests=5/20 minutes=4/15 concurrency=1/2 cost=2.5/5 cohort=10/10")
    sim.trigger_critical_gate(0.91, 0.95)
    print("GATE safety_score=0.91 minimum=0.95 result=FAIL")
    sim.record_state(0)
    sim.stop_admission(1)
    print("ADMISSION stopped=True minute=1")
    sim.preserve_evidence(2)
    sim.drain(4)
    print("DRAIN completed=3 failed_before_effect=1 unknown=op-103 minute=4")
    resolved = sim.reconcile_effects({"op-103": "completed"}, 6)
    assert resolved
    print("RECONCILE op-103=completed source=fictional_effect_lookup minute=6")
    restored = sim.restore(True, 8)
    assert restored
    print("RESTORE complete_baseline=" + sim.service_unit.identity + " minute=8")
    verified = sim.verify_postconditions(GOOD_RECOVERY_EVIDENCE, 9)
    assert verified
    labels = " ".join(name + "=" + str(value)
                      for name, value in sim.gates.items())
    print("POSTCONDITIONS " + labels)
    actual_minutes = sim.minute
    target_minutes = 10
    print(f"OBJECTIVE target_minutes={target_minutes} actual_minutes={actual_minutes} met={actual_minutes <= target_minutes}")
    sim.communicate_restoration(9)
    closed = sim.close_incident(MISSING_ACTUAL_AUTHORITY, 9)
    assert not closed
    assert sim.recovered and not sim.incident_closed
    assert not sim.candidate_release_approved
    print("INCIDENT service_recovered=True closure=pending candidate_release_approved=False")
    print("DIAGNOSIS candidate_safety_gate")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

sections.title: Meaningful negative-path tests
paragraphs: Save the following block as test_rollback_simulator.py in the same directory. It contains exactly nine unittest-discovered test methods. They cover missing effect lookup, incompatible state, failed restore, false postcondition evidence, missing closure authority, invalid phase order, every declared exposure-bound category, malformed admission values, exact Boolean evidence types, immutable manifests, and backward-time rejection. Malformed admission attempts must not change exposure or containment state. Backward reconciliation and restore attempts must preserve the original operation effects and serving unit.

Several assertions would fail if the simulator were weakened in the ways identified in the earlier version. Unconditional reconciliation or mutation before time validation would fail test_missing_effect_lookup_holds. Restore mutation before backward-time validation would fail test_failed_restore_stays_contained. Fabricated green postconditions or truthy non-Boolean evidence would fail test_bad_postcondition_blocks_recovery. Truthy non-Boolean closure authority would fail test_missing_authority_keeps_closure_pending. NaN, infinity, negative values, non-Boolean is_error, fractional concurrency, or malformed bounds would fail test_all_exposure_bounds_are_enforced.

code.label: test_rollback_simulator.py
code.code:
import unittest
from dataclasses import replace

from rollback_simulator import (
    BASELINE,
    CANDIDATE,
    ClosureEvidence,
    ExposureLimit,
    FICTIONAL_AUTHORITY_POSITIVE,
    GOOD_RECOVERY_EVIDENCE,
    MISSING_ACTUAL_AUTHORITY,
    Operation,
    Phase,
    RecoveryEvidence,
    ReleaseBounds,
    Simulation,
    TransitionError,
    make_contained_sim,
)


class RollbackTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def recovered_and_communicated(self):
        sim = make_contained_sim()
        self.assertTrue(sim.reconcile_effects({"op-103": "completed"}, 6))
        self.assertTrue(sim.restore(True, 8))
        self.assertTrue(sim.verify_postconditions(GOOD_RECOVERY_EVIDENCE, 9))
        sim.communicate_restoration(9)
        return sim

    def test_missing_effect_lookup_holds(self):
        sim = make_contained_sim()
        self.assertFalse(sim.reconcile_effects({}, 6))
        op = next(op for op in sim.operations if op.identity == "op-103")
        self.assertEqual(op.outcome, "unknown")
        self.assertFalse(op.effect_reconciled)
        self.assertEqual(sim.phase, Phase.DRAINED)
        self.assertTrue(sim.contained)
        self.assertFalse(sim.recovered)
        events_before = list(sim.events)
        with self.assertRaises(TransitionError):
            sim.reconcile_effects({"op-103": "completed"}, 5)
        self.assertEqual(op.outcome, "unknown")
        self.assertFalse(op.effect_reconciled)
        self.assertEqual(sim.phase, Phase.DRAINED)
        self.assertEqual(sim.events, events_before)

    def test_incompatible_state_refuses_restore(self):
        candidate = replace(CANDIDATE, state_schema="state-6")
        sim = make_contained_sim(candidate=candidate)
        self.assertTrue(sim.reconcile_effects({"op-103": "completed"}, 6))
        self.assertFalse(sim.restore(True, 8))
        self.assertEqual(sim.service_unit, candidate)
        self.assertTrue(sim.contained)
        self.assertFalse(sim.recovered)

    def test_failed_restore_stays_contained(self):
        sim = make_contained_sim()
        self.assertTrue(sim.reconcile_effects({"op-103": "completed"}, 6))
        self.assertFalse(sim.restore(False, 8))
        self.assertEqual(sim.service_unit, CANDIDATE)
        self.assertTrue(sim.contained)
        self.assertFalse(sim.recovered)
        backwards = make_contained_sim()
        self.assertTrue(
            backwards.reconcile_effects({"op-103": "completed"}, 6)
        )
        events_before = list(backwards.events)
        with self.assertRaises(TransitionError):
            backwards.restore(True, 5)
        self.assertEqual(backwards.service_unit, CANDIDATE)
        self.assertEqual(backwards.phase, Phase.RECONCILED)
        self.assertEqual(backwards.events, events_before)
        self.assertFalse(backwards.recovered)

    def test_bad_postcondition_blocks_recovery(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            RecoveryEvidence(
                "false", True, True, True, True, True, True, True, True
            )
        sim = make_contained_sim()
        self.assertTrue(sim.reconcile_effects({"op-103": "completed"}, 6))
        self.assertTrue(sim.restore(True, 8))
        bad = replace(GOOD_RECOVERY_EVIDENCE, telemetry=False)
        self.assertFalse(sim.verify_postconditions(bad, 9))
        self.assertFalse(sim.gates["telemetry"])
        self.assertFalse(sim.recovered)
        self.assertTrue(sim.contained)

    def test_missing_authority_keeps_closure_pending(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            ClosureEvidence("false", True, True, "Dana Okafor", "2026-09-27")
        sim = self.recovered_and_communicated()
        self.assertFalse(sim.close_incident(MISSING_ACTUAL_AUTHORITY, 10))
        self.assertTrue(sim.recovered)
        self.assertFalse(sim.incident_closed)
        self.assertFalse(sim.candidate_release_approved)

    def test_fictional_positive_authority_can_close_but_not_approve_release(self):
        sim = self.recovered_and_communicated()
        self.assertTrue(sim.close_incident(FICTIONAL_AUTHORITY_POSITIVE, 12))
        self.assertTrue(sim.incident_closed)
        self.assertFalse(sim.candidate_release_approved)

    def test_restore_before_required_phases_is_invalid(self):
        sim = Simulation()
        with self.assertRaises(TransitionError):
            sim.restore(True, 0)
        self.assertFalse(sim.recovered)

    def test_all_exposure_bounds_are_enforced(self):
        cases = [
            dict(cohort_percent=10.1, elapsed_minutes=0, concurrency=1,
                 cost_credits=0.0, is_error=False),
            dict(cohort_percent=10.0, elapsed_minutes=16, concurrency=1,
                 cost_credits=0.0, is_error=False),
            dict(cohort_percent=10.0, elapsed_minutes=0, concurrency=3,
                 cost_credits=0.0, is_error=False),
            dict(cohort_percent=10.0, elapsed_minutes=0, concurrency=1,
                 cost_credits=5.1, is_error=False),
            dict(cohort_percent=10.0, elapsed_minutes=0, concurrency=1,
                 cost_credits=0.0, is_error=True),
        ]
        for case in cases:
            with self.subTest(case=case):
                sim = Simulation()
                with self.assertRaises(ExposureLimit):
                    sim.admit(**case)
                self.assertFalse(sim.admission_open)
                self.assertTrue(sim.contained)
        sim = Simulation(bounds=ReleaseBounds(max_requests=0))
        with self.assertRaises(ExposureLimit):
            sim.admit(cohort_percent=10.0, elapsed_minutes=0,
                      concurrency=1, cost_credits=0.0)
        self.assertFalse(sim.admission_open)
        self.assertTrue(sim.contained)

        malformed = [
            dict(cohort_percent=float("nan"), elapsed_minutes=0,
                 concurrency=1, cost_credits=0.0, is_error=False),
            dict(cohort_percent=-0.1, elapsed_minutes=0,
                 concurrency=1, cost_credits=0.0, is_error=False),
            dict(cohort_percent=10.0, elapsed_minutes=float("nan"),
                 concurrency=1, cost_credits=0.0, is_error=False),
            dict(cohort_percent=10.0, elapsed_minutes=-1,
                 concurrency=1, cost_credits=0.0, is_error=False),
            dict(cohort_percent=10.0, elapsed_minutes=0,
                 concurrency=float("nan"), cost_credits=0.0,
                 is_error=False),
            dict(cohort_percent=10.0, elapsed_minutes=0,
                 concurrency=-1, cost_credits=0.0, is_error=False),
            dict(cohort_percent=10.0, elapsed_minutes=0,
                 concurrency=1.5, cost_credits=0.0, is_error=False),
            dict(cohort_percent=10.0, elapsed_minutes=0,
                 concurrency=1, cost_credits=float("nan"), is_error=False),
            dict(cohort_percent=10.0, elapsed_minutes=0,
                 concurrency=1, cost_credits=float("inf"), is_error=False),
            dict(cohort_percent=10.0, elapsed_minutes=0,
                 concurrency=1, cost_credits=-0.1, is_error=False),
            dict(cohort_percent=10.0, elapsed_minutes=0,
                 concurrency=1, cost_credits=0.0, is_error="false"),
        ]
        for case in malformed:
            with self.subTest(malformed=case):
                sim = Simulation()
                before = (
                    sim.exposure.requests,
                    sim.exposure.errors,
                    sim.exposure.cost_credits,
                    sim.admission_open,
                    sim.contained,
                )
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    sim.admit(**case)
                after = (
                    sim.exposure.requests,
                    sim.exposure.errors,
                    sim.exposure.cost_credits,
                    sim.admission_open,
                    sim.contained,
                )
                self.assertEqual(after, before)
        invalid_bounds = [
            dict(cohort_percent=float("nan")),
            dict(max_requests=1.5),
            dict(max_minutes=float("nan")),
            dict(max_concurrency=1.5),
            dict(max_cost_credits=-1.0),
            dict(max_error_percent=float("inf")),
        ]
        for values in invalid_bounds:
            with self.subTest(invalid_bounds=values):
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    ReleaseBounds(**values)

    def test_manifest_is_complete_and_immutable(self):
        required = {
            "model", "tokenizer", "runtime", "driver", "image_digest",
            "dependencies_digest", "prompt_template", "adapter",
            "endpoint_schema", "gateway_route", "identity_provider",
            "authorization_policy", "network_policy", "secret_reference",
            "infrastructure_profile", "configuration_digest",
            "evaluation_suite", "load_profile", "telemetry_config",
            "cost_profile", "state_schema", "runbook"
        }
        self.assertTrue(required.issubset(BASELINE.__dataclass_fields__))
        with self.assertRaises(Exception):
            BASELINE.state_schema = "state-6"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

sections.title: Exact filenames, run order, proposed output, and diagnosis
paragraphs: Place rollback_simulator.py, test_rollback_simulator.py, and changed_incompatible_answer.py in one directory. Run them in this order: python3.11 -m unittest -v test_rollback_simulator.py, then python3.11 rollback_simulator.py, then python3.11 changed_incompatible_answer.py. If the local Python 3.11+ executable has another name, substitute that documented executable.

The unittest command should report nine passing tests and OK. Its exact timing and test-line formatting depend on the local unittest runner, so no exact duration is predicted. Any failure is evidence that the implementation or environment differs from the supplied artifact and must be investigated.
The exact proposed standard output for rollback_simulator.py is shown below. It becomes an actual local observation only after a learner obtains it from a run.

The causal result is: the explicit safety comparison fails, admission is stopped, op-103 is resolved only because the fictional lookup contains its stable identity, the compatible complete baseline is restored, independently supplied recovery evidence passes, and the 10-minute target is met in 9 simulated minutes. Closure remains pending because actual human authority is absent. Candidate release approval remains false.

sections.title: Independent changed task: learner prompt
paragraphs: Changed requirement: the candidate safety gate now passes, but the candidate state schema is state-6 while the baseline state schema is state-5. An unrelated endpoint alert starts the response. Operation op-203 has an unknown external-effect outcome and the supplied authoritative lookup has no entry for op-203.

Determine and implement the required result. The answer must stop admission, preserve evidence, drain work, leave op-203 on HOLD without blind replay, detect the state-schema incompatibility, refuse a model-only restore, retain containment, and leave recovered and closed false. It must identify what additional evidence would permit progress.
Do not use the runnable answer in the next section until attempting the task independently.

sections.title: Separate runnable answer to the changed task
paragraphs: Save this separate answer as changed_incompatible_answer.py in the same directory as rollback_simulator.py. It imports the simulator but supplies its own changed manifest, operation ledger, assertions, and output. No network, temporary file, write, or deletion operation is performed.

The script checks incompatibility independently, then demonstrates that the missing effect lookup leaves op-203 unresolved. Restore is not invoked because reconciliation has not completed. Even if op-203 were later reconciled, the incompatible-state test in test_rollback_simulator.py proves that restore would still be refused.
The exact proposed output appears after the code. It is not an actual local observation unless produced by a learner's run.

code.label: changed_incompatible_answer.py
code.code:
from dataclasses import replace

from rollback_simulator import CANDIDATE, Operation, Phase, Simulation


def main():
    changed = replace(CANDIDATE, state_schema="state-6")
    operations = [Operation("op-203", "unknown", False)]
    sim = Simulation(candidate=changed, operations=operations)

    # The unrelated alert is the recorded incident trigger for this task.
    sim.diagnosis = "unrelated_endpoint_alert"
    sim.record_state(0)
    sim.stop_admission(1)
    sim.preserve_evidence(2)
    sim.drain(4)

    compatible = sim.compatible()
    reconciled = sim.reconcile_effects({}, 6)
    op = sim.operations[0]

    assert not compatible
    assert not reconciled
    assert op.identity == "op-203"
    assert op.outcome == "unknown"
    assert not op.effect_reconciled
    assert sim.phase is Phase.DRAINED
    assert sim.service_unit == changed
    assert sim.contained
    assert not sim.recovered
    assert not sim.incident_closed

    print("ALERT unrelated_endpoint_alert")
    print("COMPATIBILITY baseline_state=state-5 candidate_state=state-6 result=False")
    print("RECONCILE op-203=HOLD reason=missing_authoritative_lookup")
    print("RESTORE attempted=False reason=unreconciled_effect_and_incompatible_state")
    print("RESULT contained=True recovered=False closed=False")
    print("NEXT authoritative_effect_lookup_and_compatible_complete_unit_or_approved_migration")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

sections.title: Causal grading feedback for the changed task
paragraphs: Proposed exact output from changed_incompatible_answer.py is: ALERT unrelated_endpoint_alert; COMPATIBILITY baseline_state=state-5 candidate_state=state-6 result=False; RECONCILE op-203=HOLD reason=missing_authoritative_lookup; RESTORE attempted=False reason=unreconciled_effect_and_incompatible_state; RESULT contained=True recovered=False closed=False; NEXT authoritative_effect_lookup_and_compatible_complete_unit_or_approved_migration. Each semicolon here represents a new output line in the code.

Full credit requires both blocking causes. First, no authoritative op-203 lookup exists, so its effect remains unknown and reconciliation cannot complete. Second, state-6 is incompatible with the state-5 baseline, so a model-only rollback is unsafe even if the operation is later reconciled. These causes lead to continued containment, no restore, recovered false, and closed false.

Partial credit applies if admission is stopped and the state mismatch is recognized, but op-203 is replayed or treated as completed without evidence. Partial credit also applies if op-203 is correctly held but the learner fails to compare state schemas.

No credit applies if endpoint health is used to declare recovery, if op-203 is blindly replayed, if the baseline model alone is restored across the state mismatch, or if the incident is closed without recovery evidence and human authority. Progress requires an authoritative effect lookup plus either a compatible complete serving unit or an approved and tested state migration.

sections.title: Request-effect ledger and reconciliation rules
paragraphs: Request outcome and external-effect outcome must be distinguished. Completed means the intended result and effect are confirmed. Failed means failure and effect absence are independently established. Unknown means the effect cannot yet be established. Unknown is a containment state, not permission to retry.

The fictional primary lookup maps op-103 to completed. That mapping is an explicit classroom input, not a query performed by the simulator. If the mapping is absent, the simulator returns false, records an effect-hold event, keeps the operation unknown, and does not advance to the reconciled phase.

A production adapter must define the authoritative lookup system, stable identity format, identity retention, authentication, evidence ownership, idempotency guarantees, timeout behavior, and escalation path. These properties are UNKNOWN for any real deployment described only by this supplement.

code.label: Fictional ledger
code.code:
OPERATION | INITIAL OUTCOME     | LOOKUP INPUT | RESULT
op-101   | completed           | not needed   | retain evidence
op-102   | failed before effect| not needed   | retain evidence; no blind replay
op-103   | unknown             | completed    | reconciled as completed
op-203   | unknown             | missing      | HOLD; recovered remains false

sections.title: Independent recovery gates and human authority
paragraphs: Recovery evidence is supplied independently for identity, authorization, endpoint behavior, quality, safety, queue state, telemetry, cost, and visible state. verify_postconditions combines that supplied evidence with manifest identity and reconciled-operation checks. It does not set every gate to true.

Technical eligibility, release authorization, service recovery, and incident closure are four different states. Passing recovery checks does not approve the failed candidate. Restoring service does not close the incident. A modeled fictional authority fixture can test the closure transition, but it is not actual human authority.

When actual authority evidence is missing, the correct result is closure pending. When any recovery observation is absent, its value is UNKNOWN in a real evidence package and must not be translated to true in an adapter.

code.label: Minimum evidence package
code.code:
[ ] Complete immutable baseline and candidate manifests
[ ] Provenance, license, and complete-diff evidence
[ ] Evaluation, load, failure, telemetry, and cost evidence
[ ] Enforced cohort, request, time, concurrency, cost, and error bounds
[ ] Failed-gate and routing evidence
[ ] Drain or cancellation record
[ ] Stable-identity lookup for every unknown effect
[ ] Compatibility result and complete restore evidence
[ ] Independent identity, authorization, endpoint, quality, safety, queue, telemetry, cost, and visible-state results
[ ] Restoration communication
[ ] Actual human residual-risk acceptance
[ ] Required notices
[ ] Prevention owner and due date
[ ] Separate release disposition and closure record

sections.title: Provider-neutral transfer and environment-adapter limits
paragraphs: The procedure can be applied as a process template to Qwen, Meta, Microsoft Phi, Mistral, DeepSeek, Z.ai, and NVIDIA artifact families by recording complete immutable serving-unit identities rather than relying on a model label. This makes no claim about any named family's capabilities, license, format, or runtime requirements.

For every artifact family, deployment-specific evidence must establish exact model and tokenizer artifacts, runtime and driver requirements, image and dependency digests, templates, adapters, endpoint behavior, gateway routing, identity and policy, networks and secrets, infrastructure, state compatibility, evaluation slices, load behavior, telemetry, cost, and runbook validity.

A Kubernetes adapter would need to map immutable identities into image and configuration references, controller behavior, readiness, rollout limits, rollback history, routing, persistent state, operation identities, metrics, alerts, and evidence retention. Kubernetes Deployment documentation is at https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/. The supplied simulator implements none of these integrations.
Other serving or orchestration environments require equivalent mapping. No simulator result should be represented as evidence that real infrastructure was changed, restored, or qualified.

sections.title: Assumptions and omitted items
paragraphs: ASSUMPTIONS. Python 3.11 or later is available. The three files are saved together without modification. The fictional failed-before-effect operation is not counted as an error by the classroom release-bound metric. The fictional authoritative lookup for op-103 returns completed. The positive closure fixture represents fictional classroom authority only. The listed official documentation URLs and their descriptions were taken from the supplied research findings.

OMITTED. No real model deployment, local script execution, Kubernetes change, external-effect lookup, human authorization, communication dispatch, capacity test, license determination, provenance verification, state migration, or rollback execution is claimed. These cannot be delivered from the supplied fictional and offline evidence. Exact unittest duration and runner formatting are not predicted because they depend on the learner's environment.
